newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan committee passes MOF reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Japan committee passes MOF reform bill.

text.p: A Japanese parliamentary committee on Wednesday approved a bill to set up a new government inspection agency to oversee the financial sector, amid rising public anger over racketeer scandals at banks and brokerages.
The bill, approved by a special committee on administrative reform in the Lower House of parliament, aims to reform the country's powerful Ministry of Finance (MOF).

The ministry, long viewed as the pinnacle of Japan's elite bureaucracy, has come under fire for its handling of the nation's banking woes, including the secretive manner in which it deals with crises.
The bill will be submitted to a vote in the Lower House plenary session on Thursday and then passed on to the Upper House for debate, parliamentary officials said.
The main points of the agreement are as follows.
-- A fully independent body will be established under the Prime Minister's Office to take over MOF's functions of inspecting and supervising financial institutions.

-- The ministry's banking and securities bureaux will merge and take over some of the functions of the international finance bureau, although the international finance bureau will retain its basic structure for the time being.

-- The new body will oversee all financial institutions, including banks, agricultural financial firms, non-bank financial firms and labour credit associations, which are now supervised by various ministries.
The new body's inspection and supervisory functions will be shared with the Agriculture Ministry, the Labour Ministry and the Trade Ministry, which currently oversee certain financial institutions.
-- The new body must hold regular meetings with MOF to discuss financial matters from the viewpoint of maintaining order in Japan's credit markets.

-- The new agency will be responsible for handling financial failures but will be expected to consult with the finance minister on any failures that could not be handled within the framework of current procedures. Severe crises will be dealt with by the cabinet and the agency.
-- The new agency will have jurisdiction over Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission.
-- MOF's regional bureaux will retain a role in the inspection and supervision of regional financial institutions.
